title: Accept newer Claude Code patch versions instead of stopping
summary: Athena stops when the self-updating claude moves past the exact pin. I read the goal as accepting an installed claude with the same major.minor and a patch at or above the pin, recording the version actually reported. The audience is whoever runs Athena and currently repins by hand.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in the agent and xtask crates.
Unit tests with stand-in binaries; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check that a newer patch is accepted and others are still refused.
Behavior criteria run the stand-in tests.
The decision entry and error text are written for an outside reader.
One focused change to the version check and its docs.
No secrets or personal data are committed.
The compatibility rule is enforced in check_pinned and tested.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs. check_pinned (line 61) runs inside ClaudeCodeDriver::new, after refuse_nested, and compares claude_version(bin) with == to the pin. The result is stored as the driver version. Tests at about lines 612 and 855 use a stand-in binary. crates/athena-data/src/config.rs holds claude_version; crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs builds a DeferredDriver from it. xtask/src/main.rs ensure_claude (line 621) also requires an exact match before installing the pin privately with npm. No record or data file is added, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are not affected. The version is measured by running the stand-in binary's --version, the same path the driver uses.
The request is read as goal: Athena keeps running across Claude Code patch updates. Audience: whoever runs Athena. The pin in athena.toml stays and acts as the tested minimum.
The earlier readings are not replies from the user, so no user reply overrides them. I chose Reading 1 because repinning cannot run as a job, so a repin command does not remove the stop.
athena.toml is not edited. Only the check, the setup lookup that has to agree with it, and their docs change.
This loosens a refusal rule, so it refuses fewer readings, not more. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.
question: Is same major.minor with patch at or above the pin the right rule, or should any 2.x be accepted?

acceptance_criteria.text: A stand-in claude reporting a newer patch than the pin (pin 2.1.299, binary 2.1.301) is accepted by check_pinned, and the returned version is 2.1.301. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.

Tests show a binary with an older patch than the pin, a different major or minor, or an unparseable or empty version is still refused, with an error naming both the found and pinned versions. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.
ClaudeCodeDriver::new built with a pin and a binary of a different accepted patch records the binary's reported version, not the pin, and a test asserts this. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.
xtask ensure_claude uses the same compatibility rule, so a newer-patch claude on PATH is used rather than triggering an npm install. A test covers the comparison. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
`cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` pass, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

docs/decisions.md gains an entry amending D03 that states the rule, the alternatives (any 2.x, auto-repin, keep exact), what is lost (an identical version on every run), and the reversal cost. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

The refusal message and README or setup docs tell the reader that a newer patch of the pinned major.minor needs no repin. athena.toml, defaults.toml and .github/workflows are unchanged, and no secrets or personal data are committed.

out_of_scope: An xtask repin command that rewrites athena.toml
Accepting a different major or minor version
Changing how Claude Code is invoked or its flags
departures: Acceptance is lower than the reference because earlier readings split between a loosened range and a repin command.
urgent_reason: Each harness update stops every agent until a manual repin, which is wasted time and failed attempts.
hard_reason: It loosens a refusal check in the driver (check_pinned) that gates every agent run.
